tasks.short: Demonstrate safe thermal system operation to owners

steps.what: Identify installed thermal equipment and locate its operating procedures
Demonstrate start-up, shut-down, maintenance, diagnostic and safety procedures with owner teach-back

tasks.design: Configure equipment-model folders and manual bookmarks in {DOCS} for faster procedure lookup. The technician still verifies the installed model and demonstrates every procedure in person, including which diagnostic work the owner must leave to a competent technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the right instructions amid similar equipment manuals.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document indexing and bookmarks can narrow retrieval without generating instructions.
tasks.still_hard: The owner's understanding and the actual valve and control arrangement require attention on site.
tasks.human_edge: Notice unsafe understanding and adapt the demonstration before leaving.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less manual searching; teaching and safety responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.task: Improve the owner handover checklist from recurring questions
reach.learn: Plain language and the boundary between owner operation and service work

evidence.claim: Indexed equipment manuals can reduce retrieval work without replacing a practical demonstration; the allocation is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is technician preparation and owner demonstration, excluding installation, commissioning and owner learning time.

Technician reads the installed model and revision in s1 and matches the manufacturer manual; that identification and mismatch checking remain in its 60% time. Existing manufacturer manuals are source documents, not generated operating advice. Unmatched equipment uses full manual lookup or manufacturer clarification in s1.
Test native document search and bookmarks before custom code. No saving is assigned to the 85% demonstration step or existing software runtime.
unknowns: Availability of revision-specific manuals and owner language needs
research_questions: Does indexed retrieval save preparation time after equipment verification?

already_counted.description: Identify equipment and verify matched instructions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=94; gross 6 less upkeep 1 gives net 5. High assumes repeated manual searches; low assumes unfamiliar equipment requires full lookup. Demonstration time stays 85.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine safe locations for thermal subsystem components

steps.what: Survey candidate locations, pipe routes and physical access constraints
Find component dimensions, clearances and installation requirements
Determine and mark component locations after checking access, support and pipe routes

tasks.design: Use model-specific bookmarks in {DOCS} to retrieve component requirements beside the site survey. The technician retains all measurement and siting judgement; uncertain support or service conflicts are referred for design review rather than inferred by software.
tasks.enabler_now: A native document index can surface the right component sections.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden services, structural capacity and maintenance access require site evidence and competent design judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a nominally fitting location is unsafe or impossible to maintain.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in reference searching with unchanged siting authority.

reach.task: Resolve a component-location conflict before work starts
reach.learn: Communicate measured constraints and when specialist design input is needed

evidence.claim: Native indexing of component manuals can assist reference retrieval; it does not establish the safety of a location.

assumptions: Boundary ends with proposed locations, excluding structural design, installation and final commissioning sign-off.

Technician produces site measurements and observed constraints in s1 with its full baseline time. In s2 the technician identifies component model and manual revision and verifies the returned clearances; identification remains inside its 60% time. Missing model or revision means full manual lookup and escalation, never guessed dimensions.
Test native indexing before custom software. No automatic siting decision or new structured survey requirement is introduced. Existing system runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Share of work spent finding requirements
Design approval responsibilities and available site drawings
research_questions: Does model-specific retrieval shorten s2 without increasing missed clearance requirements?

already_counted.description: Identify models and check source requirements

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=94; gross 6 less upkeep 1 gives net 5. High assumes repeat component references; low assumes bespoke requirements consume retrieval savings. Survey and siting retain 85 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technician remains responsible for site judgement and practical owner instruction.
reach: Help an installation supervisor resolve location conflicts with measured evidence
role.ambitious_version: Provide better evidenced installation proposals and owner handovers without delegating safety judgement.
